what: Docker Desktop
why: Docker is absent; Linux container setup needs the owner.
fallback: Native PostgreSQL 16 is running.
resolve: 1. Install Docker Desktop from the official Docker website. 2. Enable Linux containers and launch it. 3. Run the five README Docker commands.
verify: docker compose version; prints a Compose version

what: Local secrets
why: The owner must retain the local generated password privately.
fallback: init-env ran and local login was verified.
resolve: 1. Run .\scripts\demo.ps1 init-env. 2. Run .\scripts\demo.ps1 show-demo-password locally. 3. Keep .env out of Git. Generated values are POSTGRES_PASSWORD, RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD, DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_OWNER_URL, JWT_SECRET, MASK_SECRET, GRANT_SECRET and DEMO_PASSWORD.
verify: python -m app.cli preflight; database=true and seed_ready=true

what: Optional Gemini account
why: An API key and available model require an owner account.
fallback: RULE_BASED extraction and career guidance pass without a key.
resolve: 1. Open Google AI Studio. 2. Create an API key without enabling billing. 3. Paste it into .env GEMINI_API_KEY. 4. Set GEMINI_MODEL to an available model and LLM_ENABLED=true. 5. Restart API. Live account behavior remains unverified.
verify: python -m app.cli preflight; llm_enabled=true and llm_configured=true, then verify a PDF and inspect extraction_source

what: Neon project
why: The owner must create a project and provide SSL connection strings.
fallback: Local database only.
resolve: 1. Create an empty Neon project using PostgreSQL 16. 2. Copy its direct owner URL and pooled runtime URL. 3. Follow the guarded cloud-bootstrap steps in docs/deployment.md with --students 5000. 4. Measure pg_database_size.
verify: python -m app.cli preflight; database=true, seed_ready=true

what: Render service
why: Provisioning and secrets require the owner account.
fallback: Local API works.
resolve: 1. Resolve cloud gaps in V3. 2. Create the Docker web service from render.yaml. 3. Set DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, MASK_SECRET, GRANT_SECRET and WEB_ORIGIN directly in Render. 4. Keep owner URL off the runtime service. 5. Open /api/v1/health/ready and allow cold start time.
verify: Open backend /api/v1/health/ready; HTTP200 ready

what: Vercel project
why: The owner must import a repository and accept provider terms.
fallback: Local Next web app works.
resolve: 1. Create the private GitHub repository in M7. 2. Import it in Vercel. 3. Set root apps/web and Node22. 4. Set API_INTERNAL_ORIGIN to the Render HTTPS origin, WEB_ORIGIN to the exact Vercel HTTPS origin and COOKIE_SECURE=true. 5. Align backend WEB_ORIGIN.
verify: Open frontend /login and sign in; dashboard loads through same-origin proxy

what: Private GitHub repository
why: Repository creation and pushing are owner-only by the prompt.
fallback: Local commits only; no remote is added.
resolve: 1. Create an empty private repository on GitHub. 2. Copy its SSH or HTTPS URL. 3. Run git remote add origin with that URL locally. 4. Run git push -u origin HEAD.
verify: git remote -v; shows the owner-selected repository without credentials

what: Optional tunnel
why: A tunnel process and laptop availability need owner operation.
fallback: Loopback-only demo works.
resolve: 1. Install cloudflared. 2. Run cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000. 3. Copy the returned exact HTTPS origin into .env WEB_ORIGIN. 4. Set COOKIE_SECURE=true. 5. Restart API and web with scripts/launch.py. Keep the API port private.
verify: Open tunnel /login; same-origin sign-in and CSRF mutation succeed
